meta.lede: Automate drift detection on pull requests with nextdeploy plan and zero-downtime deployments on merge with nextdeploy ship using GitHub Actions.

operations/ci-cd.body:
## Scaffold a Workflow Automatically

Generate a GitHub Actions pipeline tailored to your `nextdeploy.yml` target:

```bash
nextdeploy generate-ci
```

## Example GitHub Actions Workflow (Cloudflare Workers)

```yaml
name: NextDeploy CI/CD

on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  push:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: "22"
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm test

  plan:
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
    needs: test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Install NextDeploy
        run: curl -fsSL https://nextdeploy.org/install.sh | bash
      - name: Dry-Run Plan
        run: nextdeploy plan --detailed-exitcode
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}

  deploy:
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name == 'push'
    needs: test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Install NextDeploy
        run: curl -fsSL https://nextdeploy.org/install.sh | bash
      - name: Ship Application
        run: nextdeploy ship
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
```

For VPS deploys, add your `SSH_PRIVATE_KEY` to GitHub Secrets (loaded via `ssh-agent`) and run `nextdeploy ship` on merge to `main`.

meta.title: Monitoring & Health Checks
meta.lede: Monitor live deployments with nextdeploy status, real-time log streaming, post-deploy SmokeVerify probes, HTML deployment reports, Prometheus metrics, and automated alerts.

operations/monitoring.body:
## Real-Time Observability Overview

NextDeploy provides end-to-end monitoring across VPS bare metal, Cloudflare Workers, and AWS Lambda deployments:

1. **CLI Status & Health Probes**: Real-time snapshot of active release IDs, git hashes, uptime, memory/CPU consumption, and active ports.
2. **Unified Log Streaming**: Live log tailing that multiplexes across systemd journald (VPS), CloudWatch Logs (AWS), or Tail Workers (Cloudflare).
3. **Automated Smoke Verification (`SmokeVerify`)**: Post-deploy validation that tests HTTP response codes and latencies across public endpoints before closing cutover.
4. **Prometheus Metrics Endpoint**: Native `/metrics` exporter in `nextdeployd` for Grafana dashboards.
5. **Alert Webhooks**: Configurable Slack, Discord, or generic JSON webhooks triggered on crash or health check failure.

---

## Live Status & Log Streaming

### Inspect Live Status (`nextdeploy status`)

```bash
# Output human-readable terminal table
nextdeploy status

# Output structured JSON for AI agents and automated monitors
nextdeploy status --json
```

Sample output:
```text
App: saas-dashboard
Target: VPS (203.0.113.10)
Release: 2026-11-23_14-20-00 (Git: 8f4a1c2 - "feat: add stripe checkout")
Uptime: 4h 12m
Status: HEALTHY (HTTP 200 OK - 14ms)
Memory: 184MB / 1024MB (18.0%)
CPU: 2.1%
Active Port: 3002 (Caddy routing via 127.0.0.1:3002)
Historical Releases: 5 retained (Rollback target: 2026-11-23_10-15-00)
```

### Tail Live Logs (`nextdeploy logs`)

```bash
# Stream live logs (follow mode is default)
nextdeploy logs

# Filter by route path
nextdeploy logs --route /api/webhooks

# Stream daemon system logs
nextdeploy logs --daemon
```

- On **VPS**: Streams directly from `journalctl -u nextdeploy@<app> -f`.
- On **Cloudflare**: Connects to Cloudflare Workers Trace/Tail WebSocket stream.
- On **AWS Lambda**: Tail streams from `/aws/lambda/<app>-serverless` via AWS CloudWatch Logs Live Tail.

---

## Post-Deploy Smoke Verification (`SmokeVerify`)

After every serverless or VPS cutover, NextDeploy automatically probes your custom domain root `/` plus critical application routes before marking the deployment successful:

```yaml
# nextdeploy.yml
monitoring:
  smoke_verify:
    enabled: true
    timeout_seconds: 15
    retries: 3
    retry_delay_seconds: 2
    paths:
      - /
      - /pricing
      - /api/health
    expected_status: [200, 307] # 307 allowed for authenticated redirects
```

### Smoke Verification Rules:
- Probes run with custom user-agent `NextDeploy-SmokeVerify/1.0`.
- Automatically ignores internal Next.js error paths (`/_not-found`, `/_global-error`, `/404`, `/500`).
- If an endpoint returns 5xx status codes consecutively across retries, `nextdeploy ship` halts, triggers an automatic rollback to the previous release, and logs full trace provenance.

---

## HTML Deployment Reports

Every deployment generates a self-contained, interactive HTML architecture and DNS report inside `.nextdeploy/reports/` (gitignored so deploys never dirty your Git tree):

- `.nextdeploy/reports/<app>-<timestamp>-report.html`: Historical immutable deploy log.
- `.nextdeploy/reports/<app>-latest.html`: Always points to the current active release.

The report includes:
- Git commit metadata (author, branch, commit message, commit hash).
- Active Agent Trace session summary and prompt trails.
- Serverless resource ARN / Cloudflare ID mappings.
- Exact DNS routing verification records.
- Latency waterfall from the SmokeVerify phase.

---

## Prometheus Metrics Exporter (VPS Daemon)

The `nextdeployd` systems daemon exposes a Prometheus-compatible metrics endpoint at `http://127.0.0.1:9100/metrics` (or configured port):

```text
# HELP nextdeploy_app_up Whether the Next.js application process is healthy (1) or down (0).
# TYPE nextdeploy_app_up gauge
nextdeploy_app_up{app="saas-dashboard"} 1

# HELP nextdeploy_app_memory_rss_bytes Resident Memory Set in bytes.
# TYPE nextdeploy_app_memory_rss_bytes gauge
nextdeploy_app_memory_rss_bytes{app="saas-dashboard"} 192937984

# HELP nextdeploy_app_cpu_percent Total CPU usage percentage.
# TYPE nextdeploy_app_cpu_percent gauge
nextdeploy_app_cpu_percent{app="saas-dashboard"} 2.45

# HELP nextdeploy_http_response_time_seconds HTTP probe response time in seconds.
# TYPE nextdeploy_http_response_time_seconds histogram
nextdeploy_http_response_time_seconds_bucket{app="saas-dashboard",le="0.05"} 1420
```

Add to your `prometheus.yml`:
```yaml
scrape_configs:
  - job_name: "nextdeploy"
    static_configs:
      - targets: ["203.0.113.10:9100"]
```

---

## Automated Webhook Alerts (Slack / Discord)

Configure failure notifications in `nextdeploy.yml`:

```yaml
monitoring:
  enabled: true
  cpu_threshold: 85
  memory_threshold: 85
  alert:
    slack_webhook: ${SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL}
    discord_webhook: ${DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL}
    notify_on:
      - crash
      - healthcheck_failed
      - cutover_aborted
      - high_memory_sustained
```

When an alert triggers, NextDeploy posts a payload containing:
- Application name and environment.
- Active release ID and Git commit hash.
- The last 25 lines of application stderr.
- One-click rollback command (`nextdeploy rollback`).

meta.title: Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)
meta.lede: Comprehensive answers to architectural, operational, performance, billing, and AI agent integration questions about NextDeploy.

reference/faq.body:
## General & Architectural

### 1. How does NextDeploy compare to Vercel?
NextDeploy provides the developer ergonomics and zero-downtime cutover of Vercel, but **you own the infrastructure**:
- **Zero Bandwidth Markup:** You pay raw cloud infrastructure costs (a $4/month Hetzner/DigitalOcean VPS, or Cloudflare's $5/month Workers plan with 10M requests included) instead of Vercel's steep egress and edge compute markups.
- **No Vendor Lock-in:** Your code runs on standard Linux VPS, Cloudflare Workers, or AWS Lambda. You can switch targets anytime by modifying the `target` block in `nextdeploy.yml`.
- **Complete Infrastructure Ownership:** You retain full control over memory limits, systemd processes, database co-location, and Caddy reverse proxy rules.

---

### 2. Does NextDeploy support Next.js 15 and Next.js 16?
**Yes.** NextDeploy supports Next.js 13, 14, 15, and 16 out of the box:
- Full support for React 19, Server Actions, React Server Components (RSC), and Turbopack builds (`next build --turbo`).
- On Cloudflare Workers, NextDeploy's `nextcompile` compiler bundles the `nextserver` engine with `nodejs_compat_v2` runtime flags.
- On VPS targets, the standalone Node.js server executes directly under hardened systemd sandboxing.

---

### 3. How does Zero-Downtime Cutover work on a VPS without Docker?
NextDeploy achieves zero downtime using dual-stage health verification and atomic POSIX symlink swaps:
1. The new release is extracted into `/opt/nextdeploy/apps/<app>/releases/<timestamp>/`.
2. A new Node.js instance starts on an isolated loopback port (e.g. `3002`).
3. The `nextdeployd` daemon polls the TCP port listener and sends HTTP GET probes to `/api/health`.
4. Once verified, the daemon atomically swaps the `/opt/nextdeploy/apps/<app>/current` symlink pointer using `rename()`.
5. Caddy hot-reloads its upstream target via its internal admin API (`http://127.0.0.1:2019/load`) in under 2ms.
6. In-flight TCP requests on the previous version finish cleanly before the old process is retired.

---

### 4. What is Cumulative Static Chunk Pooling?
When users navigate your Next.js application while you deploy a new version, traditional tools wipe the old `.next/static` directory. When an active user clicks a link, their browser requests an old chunk and receives an **HTTP 404**, crashing the app with `ChunkLoadError`.

NextDeploy solves this by copying all hashed JavaScript chunks into `/opt/nextdeploy/apps/<app>/shared_static/` on every release. Old content-hashed chunks are never deleted during deployments. Active user sessions continue navigating smoothly without 404 errors.

---

### 5. What is Agent Trace & Handoff?
Agent Trace is NextDeploy's native observability layer designed for AI coding agents (Antigravity IDE, Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Kiro). It records:
- Checkpoints, prompts, model reasoning trails, and modified files into `.nextdeploy/trace/`.
- Pre-flight build failures and cutover telemetry during `nextdeploy ship`.
- When a human developer needs to take over, running `nextdeploy takeover -o` prints a concise 20-line executive brief and opens all modified files directly in `$EDITOR`.

---

## Database & State Management

### 6. How do I run database migrations (Prisma / Drizzle / Kysely)?
You can define pre-deploy hooks in `nextdeploy.yml`:

```yaml
hooks:
  pre_ship:
    - npx prisma migrate deploy
    # or: npx drizzle-kit migrate
```
If migrations fail, `nextdeploy ship` immediately halts before cutting over traffic, protecting your production database.

---

### 7. Can I run PostgreSQL or Redis directly on the same VPS?
**Yes.** Because NextDeploy runs on bare-metal Linux without container encapsulation:
- You can install PostgreSQL or Redis directly on the server (`sudo apt install postgresql redis-server`).
- Connect your Next.js application to `postgresql://user:pass@127.0.0.1:5432/dbname`.
- Enjoy sub-millisecond local Unix socket or loopback database queries without network overhead.

---

## Monorepos & CI/CD

### 8. Does NextDeploy support Turborepo, Nx, and pnpm workspaces?
**Yes.** In monorepos, specify the application subpath:

```yaml
# nextdeploy.yml
monorepo:
  app_dir: apps/web
  package_manager: pnpm
```
NextDeploy runs builds from the workspace root or designated app directory and packages the output standalone bundle accurately.

---

### 9. Can I run multiple environments (Staging vs. Production)?
**Yes.** You can define environments in `nextdeploy.yml` or use environment-specific config files:

```bash
nextdeploy ship --env staging
nextdeploy ship --env production
```
Or pass a dedicated configuration file:
```bash
nextdeploy ship -c nextdeploy.staging.yml
```

---

### 10. Do I need Docker installed on my server?
**No.** NextDeploy intentionally avoids Docker daemon overhead, container networking bridges, and virtualized file layers. It runs directly on bare metal with Linux kernel `cgroup v2` memory sandboxing and systemd process isolation.

meta.title: Limitations & Architectural Boundaries
meta.lede: Architectural boundaries, runtime execution ceilings, payload limits, and target-specific constraints across VPS, Cloudflare Workers, and AWS Lambda.

reference/limitations.body:
## Target Architecture Comparison Matrix

Before choosing a deployment target, review the architectural boundaries and constraints of each runtime environment:

| Feature / Limit | Linux VPS Bare-Metal | Cloudflare Workers | AWS Lambda Serverless |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Max Payload Size (Request / Response)** | Unlimited (Configurable in Caddy) | 100MB (Request) / Unlimited streaming | 6MB (Sync Invoke) / Unlimited streaming |
| **Execution Timeout** | Unlimited (Long-running processes allowed) | 30s CPU time (Unlimited I/O wait on Paid) | 15 minutes (Default: 30s) |
| **Bundle Size Ceiling** | Unlimited (Constrained only by disk) | 10MB compressed (3MB on Free plan) | 250MB uncompressed / 50MB zipped |
| **WebSockets Support** | Full bidirectional persistent WebSockets | Supported via WebSocket Hibernation API | Supported via API Gateway WebSockets |
| **Node.js Native C++ Addons (`.node`)** | Full support (compiled on host Linux) | Not supported (`workerd` / Wasm only) | Supported (compiled for `amzn2` / `al2023`) |
| **Persistent Disk Storage** | Local NVMe SSD / `/opt/nextdeploy` | None (Ephemeral memory; use R2/KV) | 512MB–10GB ephemeral `/tmp` or EFS mount |
| **Zero-Downtime Rollbacks** | Instant (POSIX symlink swap in <10ms) | Instant (Worker script alias flip) | Instant (Lambda function alias routing) |
| **Cold Starts** | 0ms (Always-on hot process) | <5ms global edge cold start | 150ms–400ms (Reduced with ARM64 + provisioned) |

---

## Target-Specific Constraints & Details

### 1. Cloudflare Workers Target

NextDeploy compiles your Next.js application into a standard Cloudflare Worker utilizing the `nextserver` runtime engine and Cloudflare's `nodejs_compat_v2` compatibility flag:

- **Script Size Limit (10MB):** Cloudflare enforces a strict 10MB compressed bundle limit.
  - *NextDeploy Optimization:* NextDeploy automatically extracts all static assets (`.next/static/*` and `public/*`) and uploads them directly to Cloudflare R2 before compiling the Worker bundle. This ensures only server logic is bundled into the script.
  - *Mitigation for Monoliths:* If heavy server dependencies (e.g. headless browsers, PDF generators) exceed 10MB, externalize them or deploy that specific microservice to VPS or AWS Lambda.
- **Node.js Native C++ Binaries:** Cloudflare's `workerd` edge runtime executes V8 JavaScript and WebAssembly. It does not load `.node` compiled C++ modules (such as non-Wasm `sharp` or native `bcrypt`). NextDeploy shims cryptographic and standard APIs using Web Crypto and Pure-JS implementations.
- **Dynamic Code Evaluation:** `eval()` and `new Function()` with dynamic strings are restricted in standard worker mode for security.

---

## 2. AWS Serverless Target

NextDeploy packages the Next.js standalone server into an AWS Lambda function with Amazon CloudFront distribution:

- **250MB Uncompressed Package Limit:** AWS Lambda limits the uncompressed deployment artifact to 250MB. NextDeploy separates static chunks into S3 with CloudFront Origin Access Control (OAC), keeping the core Lambda function package between 18MB and 35MB.
- **6MB Synchronous Payload Ceiling:** AWS API Gateway and Lambda synchronous invocations return `413 Request Entity Too Large` if request or response bodies exceed 6MB.
  - *Workaround:* For file uploads, use S3 Presigned URLs so user browsers upload directly to S3.
  - *For Large Downloads:* NextDeploy enables Lambda Response Streaming, bypassing the 6MB response limit.
- **Lambda Ephemeral File Storage:** The root filesystem is read-only. Writable scratch space is limited to `/tmp` (configurable from 512MB up to 10GB). Do not store persistent user uploads in `/tmp`.

---

## 3. VPS Bare-Metal Target

Running on Linux VPS bare metal provides complete freedom without serverless restrictions, with the following operational considerations:

- **Single Host by Default:** Standard `nextdeploy.yml` configurations target a single server IP. While single NVMe VPS instances easily handle thousands of requests per second, multi-region high availability requires deploying to multiple server targets behind an external DNS load balancer (such as Cloudflare Load Balancing).
- **Static Chunk Disk Accumulation:** NextDeploy's Cumulative Static Chunk Pooling (`shared_static`) intentionally retains old hashed JavaScript chunks across releases to prevent client-side `ChunkLoadError` 404 crashes. The daemon automatically limits release directories to the last 5 builds via an immutable ring buffer.
- **Server Maintenance:** Unlike serverless platforms where underlying OS security patches are managed by the cloud provider, you are responsible for Linux kernel updates and security patches (`apt update && apt upgrade`).

meta.title: Troubleshooting
meta.lede: Fast fixes for the most common build, Cloudflare API, DNS, SSH, runtime, and Agent Trace issues encountered when deploying Next.js apps with NextDeploy.

reference/troubleshooting.body:
## Cloudflare Deploy Issues

### `Error: KV PUT failed: 429 Too Many Requests` (`checkRateLimit`)
If your deployed Cloudflare Worker throws a `500 Internal Server Error` with:

```text
Error: KV PUT failed: 429 Too Many Requests
    at async checkRateLimit (worker.mjs:...)
    at async runGuard (worker.mjs:...)
```

- **Cause:** Cloudflare Workers KV enforces a hard limit of **1 `PUT` per second to the same key** (plus 1,000 `PUT`s/day on the Free plan). Navigating Next.js pages fires both the document request and concurrent `<Link>` RSC prefetches within the same second, hitting the same `rl:<ip>:<windowId>` rate-limit key.
- **Fix 1 — Scope rate limiting away from static/docs routes:** Exclude marketing and documentation routes in `nextdeploy.yml` and target `rate_limit.paths` to sensitive routes:
  ```yaml
  serverless:
    cloudflare:
      protection:
        enabled: true
        public_paths: ["/", "/login", "/docs", "/docs/*"]
        rate_limit:
          kv_binding: RATE_LIMIT
          requests_per_minute: 60
          paths: ["/api/*", "/app/*"]
  ```
- **Fix 2 — Upgrade/rebuild the NextDeploy binary:** Current builds of `shared/nextcompile/runtime_src/guard.mjs` coalesce `kv.put` writes to at most once every `1,100ms` per key per isolate, run writes through `ctx.waitUntil(...)`, and catch KV `429` errors gracefully so traffic never 500s. Rebuild your `nextdeploy` CLI binary (`nextdeploy update` or `go build`) and re-run `nextdeploy ship`.

### Next.js 16.4+ Worker 500: `TypeError: l2 is not a function` / `Cannot set property setImmediate`
If every route (`/`, `/docs`, `/api/health`) returns `HTTP 500 Internal Server Error` after upgrading to Next.js `16.4+` and live Cloudflare logs (`nextdeploy logs`) or local smoke tests show either:

```text
TypeError: l2 is not a function
    at r0.loadManifests (...)
```

or:

```text
Error: Failed to load external module next/dist/compiled/next-server/app-page-turbo.runtime.prod.js:
TypeError: Cannot set property setImmediate of #<Object> which has only a getter
```

- **Cause:**
  1. Next.js `16.4+` imports `evalManifestFromRelativePath` (and relies on `handleMissing` returning `undefined`) from `next/dist/server/load-manifest.external.js`. Older Worker shims only exported `evalManifest` and `loadManifestFromRelativePath`.
  2. Next.js `16.4+` executes `install()` at module load inside `next/dist/server/node-environment-extensions/fast-set-immediate.external.js`, assigning `require("node:timers").setImmediate = patchedSetImmediate`, which throws on esbuild's read-only ESM namespace wrapper in Cloudflare Workers.
- **Fix:** Update/rebuild the `nextdeploy` CLI binary (`nextdeploy update` or `go build -o ./bin/nextdeploy ./cli`) so `cli/internal/serverless/cloudflare/adapter/adapter.go` and `shared/nextcompile/runtime_src/next_shims/fast_set_immediate.mjs` include the updated `load-manifest.external.js` and `fast-set-immediate.external.js` shims, then re-run `nextdeploy ship`.

### `purge_cache: 401 Unauthorized` (non-fatal)
Your deployment succeeded, but your Cloudflare API token is missing the **Zone → Cache Purge: Purge** permission. Add that permission in the Cloudflare dashboard to enable automatic edge cache purges.

### `duplicate Worker binding name`
An `.env` or Doppler secret key has the same name as a declared Cloudflare binding (e.g. `ASSETS`, `DB`, `RATE_LIMIT`). Rename the binding or remove the conflicting key from `.env`.

### `script size exceeds 10MB limit` (Worker Script Limit Exceeded)
Cloudflare enforces a **10MB compressed script size limit** on the Paid Plan (3MB on Free). While NextDeploy automatically strips `.next/static` and `public/` into R2, extremely large Node.js server dependencies can inflate the worker bundle.
- **Fix 1: Externalize heavy server dependencies:** In `nextdeploy.yml`:
  ```yaml
  serverless:
    cloudflare:
      bundle:
        external:
          - "@aws-sdk/*"
          - "canvas"
  ```
- **Fix 2: Inspect standalone build output:** Check which node modules are bloated inside `.next/standalone/node_modules`. Ensure heavy development tools are in `devDependencies` rather than `dependencies`.
- **Fix 3: Verify asset offload:** Ensure `serverless.cloudflare.resources.r2` has an `assets_bucket` configured so static media isn't bundled into code.

### Forcing or Comparing Worker Engines
If you want to explicitly force the `nextserver` or `legacy` engine for debugging:

```bash
NEXTDEPLOY_CF_ENGINE=nextserver nextdeploy ship
NEXTDEPLOY_CF_ENGINE=legacy nextdeploy ship
```

### Local Reproduction of a Cloudflare Worker Bundle
Test your compiled Worker locally against Node before uploading:

```bash
NEXTDEPLOY_CF_ENGINE=nextserver NEXTDEPLOY_TEST_STANDALONE=/path/to/your-app/.next/standalone \
  go test -v ./cli/internal/serverless/cloudflare/adapter -run TestBuildWorkerBundle_RealStandaloneSmoke
```

---

## Next.js Runtime & Build Errors

### `DYNAMIC_SERVER_USAGE` Error during prerendering
This occurs when a page or component uses dynamic functions (such as `cookies()`, `headers()`, or `searchParams`) without marking the route segment dynamic.
- **Fix:** Add route segment config at the top of the route file:
  ```typescript
  export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic';
  ```
  Or ensure dynamic functions are wrapped inside a `<Suspense>` boundary if static shell rendering is desired.

### `NEXT_NOT_FOUND` or `NEXT_REDIRECT` uncaught exception in edge middleware
Next.js handles `notFound()` and `redirect()` by throwing internal errors that must be caught by the Next.js runtime.
- **Fix:** If your custom middleware or route handler wraps downstream calls in `try/catch`, ensure you re-throw Next.js internal errors:
  ```typescript
  try {
    // business logic
  } catch (error) {
    if (error && typeof error === 'object' && 'digest' in error) {
      throw error; // Let Next.js handle NEXT_REDIRECT or NEXT_NOT_FOUND
    }
    // log application error
  }
  ```

### `Cannot find name 'R2Bucket'` or `'KVNamespace'` during `next build`
Install `@cloudflare/workers-types` as a dev dependency (or type bindings as `any` / minimal interfaces in `lib/env.ts`) so `next build`'s TypeScript check resolves Cloudflare binding types cleanly:
```bash
npm install -D @cloudflare/workers-types
```
Add to `tsconfig.json`:
```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "types": ["@cloudflare/workers-types/2023-07-01"]
  }
}
```

### Doppler CLI prints help text instead of running `nextdeploy`
Include `--` before the command so Doppler doesn't parse `nextdeploy` flags:

```bash
doppler run -- nextdeploy ship
```

---

## AWS Serverless Deploy Issues

### `504 Gateway Timeout` on Lambda Invocations
- **Cause:** Lambda cold start exceeded CloudFront or API Gateway's 30-second origin response timeout.
- **Fix 1:** Increase memory allocation in `nextdeploy.yml` (`memory: 1792` or `2048`). AWS scales CPU linearly with allocated RAM, cutting initialization cold starts by up to 60%.
- **Fix 2:** Check database connection pooling. Ensure your Prisma/Drizzle connection pool allows fast reconnects or uses AWS RDS Proxy.
- **Fix 3:** Enable NextDeploy Lambda Response Streaming so the HTTP response headers and initial HTML chunk flush immediately to CloudFront.

### `RequestEntityTooLargeException: Request must be smaller than 6MB`
Synchronous Lambda invocations have a strict 6MB payload limit.
- **Fix:** If uploading large files, generate S3 Presigned URLs using the AWS SDK so browsers upload directly to S3 without passing payloads through Next.js server actions.

### ACM validation stuck in "Pending Validation"
If your domain uses Cloudflare DNS in front of AWS CloudFront, make sure the ACM validation CNAME records are set to **DNS only (gray cloud)**, not proxied (orange cloud). Cloudflare proxying alters CNAME resolution and blocks AWS's automated certificate verification.

---

## VPS & SSH Issues

### `Host key verification failed` or `Permission denied (publickey)`
- **Host Key Verification Failed:** The VPS host key changed (e.g. server was rebuilt). Update your known hosts file:
  ```bash
  ssh-keygen -R <server-ip>
  ```
- **Permission Denied:** Verify your SSH identity file matches the configured user:
  ```bash
  ssh -i ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 root@<server-ip>
  ```
  Ensure permissions on your private key are strict (`chmod 600 ~/.ssh/id_ed25519`).

### TLS certificate not issuing on VPS (Caddy error)
1. Confirm your domain's `A` record points to the VPS IP (`dig example.com A +short`).
2. Verify ports `80` and `443` are open in your server firewall:
   ```bash
   sudo ufw status
   sudo ufw allow 80/tcp
   sudo ufw allow 443/tcp
   ```
3. Inspect Caddy logs:
   ```bash
   journalctl -u caddy -n 100 --no-pager
   ```

### Node.js memory exhaustion (`SIGKILL` / Exit code 137)
On low-memory VPS instances (1GB RAM), Next.js builds or high traffic spikes can trigger the Linux kernel Out-Of-Memory (OOM) killer.
- **Fix 1: Add a Swapfile:**
  ```bash
  sudo fallocate -l 2G /swapfile
  sudo chmod 600 /swapfile
  sudo mkswap /swapfile
  sudo swapon /swapfile
  ```
- **Fix 2: Set memory limits in `nextdeploy.yml`:**
  ```yaml
  vps:
    resources:
      memory_limit: 1024M
  ```

---

## Agent Trace & Handoff Troubleshooting

### Checkpoint Corruption or Missing Trace
If an AI coding agent crashed mid-turn or an interrupted Git rebase disrupted `.nextdeploy/trace/`:
- Check trace health:
  ```bash
  nextdeploy trace status
  ```
- If the index is out of sync, view the latest raw checkpoints directly:
  ```bash
  ls -lat .nextdeploy/trace/checkpoints/
  cat .nextdeploy/trace/events.jsonl | tail -n 20
  ```
- To reset or re-initialize a corrupted active trace session without losing git history:
  ```bash
  rm -f .nextdeploy/trace/active_session.json
  nextdeploy trace checkpoint -m "Manual recovery checkpoint"
  ```

### Web UI Port Conflict (`:4044` already in use)
If port 4044 is occupied by an existing process:
```bash
nextdeploy trace ui --port 4055
```
Or kill the stale process:
```bash
lsof -ti :4044 | xargs kill -9
```

---

## MCP Server Troubleshooting

### Cursor or Claude Code reports "MCP server disconnected"
1. Verify the `nextdeploy-mcp` binary is compiled and available in your `PATH`:
   ```bash
   which nextdeploy-mcp || go build -o /usr/local/bin/nextdeploy-mcp ./mcp
   ```
2. Verify `nextdeploy-mcp` executes cleanly on `stdio`:
   ```bash
   echo '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"tools/list","id":1}' | nextdeploy-mcp
   ```
3. In Cursor or Claude Code MCP settings, ensure `command` points to the absolute path of `nextdeploy-mcp` and `cwd` is set to your workspace root directory.

meta.title: Doppler Integration
meta.lede: Inject encrypted secrets seamlessly into nextdeploy plan, build, and ship using Doppler across local development, staging branches, and automated CI/CD pipelines.

secrets/doppler.body:
## Why Use Doppler with NextDeploy

NextDeploy is designed with a **Zero-Secrets-on-Disk** security philosophy. Storing plaintext `.env` or `.env.production` files on developer laptops or remote servers risks accidental Git commits and secret leakage.

By integrating Doppler:
- Secrets are fetched just-in-time into process memory during `nextdeploy plan` and `nextdeploy ship`.
- `nextdeploy.yml` natively interpolates `${ENV_VAR}` placeholders from the injected Doppler environment.
- On VPS deployments, secrets are written directly to systemd environment files with `chmod 600` permissions or injected via the NextDeploy encrypted vault.
- On Cloudflare and AWS, secrets are automatically synchronized to Worker environment variables or AWS Secrets Manager.

---

## The `--` Syntax Rule

When invoking NextDeploy through Doppler CLI, always include the `--` argument separator:

```bash
# Correct: doppler passes all flags directly to nextdeploy
doppler run -- nextdeploy plan
doppler run -- nextdeploy ship
doppler run -- nextdeploy status

# Incorrect: Doppler attempts to parse nextdeploy flags
doppler run nextdeploy ship --env prod   # Doppler might intercept --env!
```

---

## Configuration Example

Declare your secret bindings in `nextdeploy.yml` using `${VARIABLE_NAME}` syntax:

```yaml
app_name: saas-web
target:
  type: serverless
  provider: cloudflare

serverless:
  cloudflare:
    account_id: ${CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID}
    api_token: ${CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN}
    zone_name: example.com
    resources:
      hyperdrive:
        - name: primary-db
          binding: HYPERDRIVE
          origin: ${DATABASE_URL}
      r2:
        assets_bucket: saas-assets
        custom_buckets:
          - name: saas-uploads
            binding: UPLOADS

env:
  NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL: ${NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL}
  STRIPE_SECRET_KEY: ${STRIPE_SECRET_KEY}
  AUTH_SECRET: ${AUTH_SECRET}
```

---

## Multi-Environment Workflows (Dev, Staging, Prod)

Doppler provides first-class environment configurations (`dev`, `stg`, `prd`). You can target specific configurations using Doppler's `--config` flag:

```bash
# Deploy to Staging using Staging credentials
doppler run --config stg -- nextdeploy ship

# Deploy to Production using Production credentials
doppler run --config prd -- nextdeploy ship
```

---

## Integrating Doppler in GitHub Actions CI/CD

Store a single `DOPPLER_TOKEN` service token in GitHub Actions Repository Secrets:

```yaml
name: Deploy Next.js to Cloudflare via NextDeploy & Doppler

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout Code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install Doppler CLI
        uses: dopplerhq/cli-action@v3

      - name: Install NextDeploy
        run: curl -fsSL https://nextdeploy.org/install.sh | bash

      - name: Run NextDeploy Preflight Plan
        env:
          DOPPLER_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.DOPPLER_TOKEN_PROD }}
        run: doppler run -- nextdeploy plan --detailed-exitcode

      - name: Deploy Production Release
        env:
          DOPPLER_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.DOPPLER_TOKEN_PROD }}
        run: doppler run -- nextdeploy ship
```

---

## Troubleshooting Doppler Invocations

- **`DOPPLER_TOKEN not found`:** Ensure `doppler login` has been run locally, or `DOPPLER_TOKEN` is exported in your environment.
- **`Variable ${NAME} is empty`:** Check your Doppler dashboard for the active project/config to ensure the variable is defined and unlocked.
- **Token Scope:** Ensure the Doppler service token has read access to the relevant Doppler Project and Config.

meta.title: Local Authenticated Encryption
meta.lede: Mathematical and implementation details of NextDeploy's ChaCha20-Poly1305 and AES-256-GCM authenticated secret encryption.

secrets/encryption.body:
## Cryptographic Primitives

NextDeploy utilizes **Authenticated Encryption with Associated Data (AEAD)** to ensure both confidentiality and cryptographic integrity for all stored secrets:

1. **Primary Cipher**: `ChaCha20-Poly1305` (RFC 8439).
   - High speed on ARM64 and x86_64 architectures without hardware AES acceleration.
   - Immune to cache-timing attacks.
2. **Alternative Cipher**: `AES-256-GCM` (NIST SP 800-38D).
   - Compliant with strict enterprise FIPS requirements.
3. **Key Derivation Function (KDF)**: `Argon2id` (RFC 9106) with:
   - Memory: 64 MB (`memory = 64 * 1024`)
   - Iterations: 3
   - Parallelism: 4
   - Salt: 16 cryptographically secure random bytes generated via `crypto/rand`.

---

## Vault File Format (`.secrets`)

When you run `nextdeploy secrets set`, the secret payload is encrypted into a binary vault file:

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    VAULT BINARY LAYOUT                       │
├──────────────┬──────────────┬──────────────┬─────────────────┤
│ Magic (4B)   │ Version (1B) │ Salt (16B)   │ Nonce (12B)     │
├──────────────┴──────────────┴──────────────┴─────────────────┤
│ Ciphertext + Poly1305 / GCM Authentication Tag (Variable)    │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

1. **Magic Bytes**: `0x4E 0x44 0x53 0x43` (`NDSC` for NextDeploy Secret Container).
2. **Version**: Current specification version (`0x01`).
3. **Salt**: Unique random salt for Argon2id key derivation.
4. **Nonce**: 96-bit (12-byte) random initialization vector. A new nonce is generated for every single write operation.
5. **Tag**: 128-bit authentication tag. Any tampering or bit-flipping causes decryption to fail immediately.

---

## Key Management & Environment Variables

NextDeploy resolves the master encryption key from the following sources in order:

1. Environment variable: `NEXTDEPLOY_ENCRYPTION_KEY` (64-character hexadecimal string).
2. Secure local key file: `~/.nextdeploy/master.key` (permission `0600`).
3. Automated key generation: If neither exists, NextDeploy generates a cryptographically random 256-bit key and saves it to `~/.nextdeploy/master.key`.

### CI/CD Deployment Key
In automated CI/CD pipelines (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI), add `NEXTDEPLOY_ENCRYPTION_KEY` to your repository secrets. During deployment, the CLI uses this key to decrypt secrets in memory and inject them directly into your deployment target.

---

## Key Updates & Secret Synchronization

To update your deployment keys or re-sync encrypted values across targets:

```bash
# Load updated variables from a secure .env file
nextdeploy secrets load .env.production

# Synchronize secrets to the active target
nextdeploy secrets sync
```
NextDeploy securely writes secrets into memory or provider vaults and updates remote daemon / worker state.

meta.title: AWS Secrets Manager Lambda Extension
meta.lede: Secure in-memory secret retrieval at Lambda cold start without environment variable plaintext exposure.

secrets/lambda-extension.body:
## The Plaintext Environment Variable Vulnerability

A common security anti-pattern in serverless architectures is setting secrets directly in Lambda environment variables (`process.env.DATABASE_URL`).

This exposes sensitive credentials in multiple attack surfaces:
- Plaintext visibility in the AWS Management Console to anyone with read-only IAM permissions.
- Inadvertent logging in AWS CloudTrail API event histories (`GetFunction`, `UpdateFunctionConfiguration`).
- Permanent preservation across all published immutable Lambda version snapshots.

NextDeploy mitigates this vulnerability by utilizing the **AWS Parameters and Secrets Lambda Extension**.

---

## Extension Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    SM["AWS Secrets Manager"] -->|"SigV4 Fetch at Cold Start"| Ext["AWS Secrets Lambda Extension Layer"]
    Ext -->|"Local In-Memory Cache"| Daemon["Local HTTP Daemon (http://localhost:2773)"]
    Daemon -->|"Local Fast Path 1ms"| NextApp["Next.js Server / Bridge"]
```

---

## How It Works

1. **Automated Layer Mounting**: When `serverless.provider: aws` is deployed, NextDeploy automatically attaches the AWS-managed Secrets Manager Extension ARN matching your architecture (`arm64` or `x86_64`) and region.
2. **Local HTTP Daemon**: The extension runs as an independent companion process inside the Lambda execution environment, listening on `http://localhost:2773`.
3. **In-Memory Caching**: During cold start, the NextDeploy bridge fetches all application secrets via a local loopback HTTP call (`GET http://localhost:2773/systemsmanager/parameters/get/?name=...`). The extension caches secrets in memory for the lifetime of the Lambda instance.
4. **Zero Outbound Latency During Warm Invocations**: After cold start, subsequent user requests read from memory with **0ms outbound network latency**.

---

## Configuration

In `nextdeploy.yml`:

```yaml
target:
  type: serverless
  provider: aws

serverless:
  provider: aws
  region: us-east-1
  kms_key_id: "alias/production-secrets-key" # Optional custom customer KMS key
  allow_secrets_in_env: false # Defaults to false for strict security
```

> [!WARNING]
> Only set `allow_secrets_in_env: true` if your deployment IAM role lacks `lambda:GetLayerVersion` permissions and you explicitly accept that secrets will be persisted in published Lambda versions.

meta.title: Secrets Management Overview
meta.lede: End-to-end secret lifecycle: local authenticated encryption, cloud synchronization, and runtime injection without plaintext exposure.

secrets/overview.body:
## Principles of Secret Security

Managing production secrets for Next.js applications (database connection strings, Stripe API keys, OAuth client secrets, authentication tokens) is critical. NextDeploy adheres to strict security invariants:

1. **Zero Plaintext Secrets in Repositories**: Plaintext secrets are never committed to git.
2. **Authenticated Symmetric Encryption**: Secrets stored locally or in CI/CD are encrypted with **ChaCha20-Poly1305** (or AES-256-GCM) authenticated encryption with unique nonces.
3. **Least-Privilege Cloud Ingestion**:
   - On **VPS**: Secrets are injected into the daemon's memory space and passed to systemd processes via secure IPC pipes; never stored unencrypted in `/etc/environment` or bash history.
   - On **Cloudflare Workers**: Secrets are written directly to encrypted Worker Secret bindings via the Cloudflare API.
   - On **AWS**: Stored in AWS Secrets Manager and retrieved in-memory via the Lambda Extension.

---

## Secret Providers Supported

NextDeploy supports multiple secret providers configured in `nextdeploy.yml`:

```yaml
secrets:
  provider: local # 'local', 'doppler', or 'aws'
  encryption: chacha20 # 'chacha20' or 'aes256'
```

| Provider | Best For | Storage Location | Key Commands |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`local` (Default)** | Solo developers, fast iteration, self-hosted | Local encrypted vault (`.secrets`) | `nextdeploy secrets set/get/list` |
| **`doppler`** | Teams, centralized secret rotation, multi-env | Doppler Secret Platform | `doppler run -- nextdeploy ship` |
| **`aws`** | AWS enterprise compliance, multi-account | AWS Secrets Manager | Automated via Lambda Extension |
| **`cloudflare`** | Edge workers | Cloudflare Encrypted Worker Secrets | Reconciled during `nextdeploy ship` |

---

## Secret Operations CLI

Manage secrets effortlessly with the unified CLI:

```bash
# Set an encrypted secret
nextdeploy secrets set DATABASE_URL=postgres://user:pass@ep-cool.us-east-1.neon.tech/db

# View all secret keys (values masked by default)
nextdeploy secrets list

# Retrieve a secret value
nextdeploy secrets get DATABASE_URL

# Load variables from a .env file into the secret store
nextdeploy secrets load .env.production

# Remove a secret permanently
nextdeploy secrets unset OLD_TOKEN

# Sync secrets to the remote daemon or cloud provider
nextdeploy secrets sync

# Preview or remove orphaned remote secrets
nextdeploy secrets prune --apply
```

---

## Pre-Deploy Integration Verification

During `nextdeploy plan` and `nextdeploy ship`, NextDeploy's introspection engine (`shared/nextcore`) cross-references the external services detected in your compiled bundles with your configured secrets:

- If Stripe SDK is detected in `node_modules` but `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` is missing, NextDeploy warns immediately.
- If Supabase or Prisma is detected but `DATABASE_URL` is empty, deployment is halted before pushing broken code to production.

meta.title: Zero-Downtime Cutover
meta.lede: How NextDeploy achieves true zero-downtime releases on Linux VPS hosts using ephemeral port allocation, dual-stage TCP/HTTP health probes, atomic POSIX renameat() symlink swaps, and graceful connection draining.

vps/atomic-cutover.body:
## Release Isolation & Ephemeral Port Allocation

Every `nextdeploy ship` builds into a brand-new immutable release directory:

```text
/opt/nextdeploy/apps/my-app/releases/2026-11-23_14-20-00/
```

1. `nextdeployd` inspects active listening ports and assigns an idle internal loopback port (e.g. `127.0.0.1:3002` while the active release runs on `:3001`).
2. The incoming release boots inside its own systemd scope under its configured `cgroup v2` memory limit.
3. A temporary symlink `current.tmp` is created pointing at the new release directory.

---

## Dual-Stage Health Probing

No live traffic shifts until both stages pass:

### Stage 1: TCP Port Probe
Verifies the Node.js HTTP listener is bound and accepting connections — catching startup crashes, missing env vars, or syntax errors immediately.

### Stage 2: HTTP Semantic Probe
Issues HTTP `GET` requests to `deployment.healthcheck.path` (default `/api/health`):

```http
GET /api/health HTTP/1.1
Host: 127.0.0.1:3002
```

The deploy advances only when the endpoint returns `200 OK` within `timeout` (default `5s`) across `retries` attempts.

---

## Atomic Symlink Swap & Connection Draining

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Client["Incoming Client Requests (:443)"] --> Caddy["Caddy Reverse Proxy + Coraza WAF"]
    Caddy -.->|"1. In-flight requests drain"| OldNode["Old Release on 127.0.0.1:3001"]
    Caddy ==>|"2. New requests cut over"| NewNode["New Release on 127.0.0.1:3002"]
    Daemon["nextdeployd"] -->|"current.tmp -> current rename()"| Link["current -> releases/1763890000-a1b2c3d"]
    Daemon -->|"Sandbox validate & reload Caddy"| Caddy
    Daemon -->|"SIGTERM (TimeoutStopSec=10s)"| OldNode
```

### The 4-Step Cutover Protocol:
1. `nextdeployd` validates and reloads Caddy's fragment (`/etc/caddy/nextdeploy.d/<app>.caddy`) pointing at the healthy candidate port.
2. Executes an atomic POSIX `os.Rename("current.tmp", "current")` swap pointing `current` to the new release directory.
3. Caddy immediately routes all new incoming requests to the new release on `:3002`.
4. Stops the previous systemd unit (`SIGTERM`, `TimeoutStopSec=10s`, `KillMode=control-group`), allowing in-flight requests to finish cleanly before terminating.

If health checks fail at any point, the active release stays untouched and zero users see an error.

meta.title: Cumulative Static Chunk Pooling
meta.lede: Permanently eliminating Next.js ChunkLoadError 404 crashes for active user sessions across production updates using shared_static.

vps/chunk-pooling.body:
## The Client-Side `ChunkLoadError` Problem

Next.js utilizes aggressive code-splitting. Every page, component, and dynamic import is compiled into an immutable, content-hashed JavaScript chunk:
- `_next/static/chunks/app/dashboard-8f92a1.js`
- `_next/static/chunks/684-2a1d9e.js`

In traditional deployment pipelines (or naïve Docker container replacements):
1. User A visits your Next.js application at version `v1.0`. The HTML shell is loaded into their browser, referencing chunk `dashboard-8f92a1.js`.
2. While User A is reading the page, you deploy `v1.1`. The new deployment deletes or replaces the previous `.next/static` directory with fresh chunks (`dashboard-3c4b5e.js`).
3. User A clicks the "Dashboard" navigation tab. Their browser requests the old chunk:
   ```text
   GET /_next/static/chunks/app/dashboard-8f92a1.js HTTP/2
   ```
4. The server cannot find the file and returns **HTTP 404 Not Found**.
5. The application crashes in User A's browser with the unhandled runtime error:
   ```text
   ChunkLoadError: Loading chunk app/dashboard-8f92a1 failed.
   (missing: https://example.com/_next/static/chunks/app/dashboard-8f92a1.js)
   ```

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor User as Active User Browser
    participant Server as Web Server (Legacy)
    User->>Server: 1. Load HTML v1.0 (references chunk-A.js)
    Server-->>User: Returns HTML v1.0
    Note over Server: Deploy v1.1 wipes old chunks!
    User->>Server: 2. Navigate to /dashboard (requests chunk-A.js)
    Server-->>User: 3. HTTP 404 Not Found!
    Note over User: ChunkLoadError: Crash!
```

---

## How NextDeploy Solves It: `shared_static`

NextDeploy permanently eliminates this issue on VPS bare metal by implementing a **Cumulative Static Chunk Pool**:

```text
/opt/nextdeploy/apps/<app>/
├── current -> releases/v1.1/
├── releases/
│   ├── v1.0/
│   └── v1.1/
└── shared_static/               <── Cumulative Static Chunk Pool
    ├── chunks/
    │   ├── app/dashboard-8f92a1.js   (Retained from v1.0)
    │   └── app/dashboard-3c4b5e.js   (Added in v1.1)
    ├── media/
    └── css/
```

---

## The Synchronization Protocol

1. **Build Phase:** Next.js compiles the application, creating hashed assets in `.next/static/`.
2. **Transfer Phase:** The release archive is unpacked into `/opt/nextdeploy/apps/<app>/releases/<new-id>/`.
3. **Cumulative Pooling (`nextdeployd`):** The daemon copies all files from `.next/static/` into `/opt/nextdeploy/apps/<app>/shared_static/` using an additive synchronization algorithm (`rsync --ignore-existing` semantics):
   - Existing chunks are **never deleted or overwritten**.
   - Because chunks are content-hashed, identical files share the exact same hash, while modified components receive new unique hashes.
4. **Caddy Static Routing:** Caddy serves all requests matching `/_next/static/*` directly from `/opt/nextdeploy/apps/<app>/shared_static/` using high-speed Linux kernel `sendfile`.
5. **Zero 404s:** Active users who opened the site before deployment continue navigating seamlessly across pages.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Build["Next.js Build Output: .next/static"] --> Sync["Additive Sync Engine"]
    Sync --> Pool[("Cumulative Pool: /shared_static")]
    Caddy["Caddy Reverse Proxy"] -->|"/_next/static/*"| Pool
    Pool -->|"Retains v1.0 Chunks"| UserOld["Active Users on v1.0"]
    Pool -->|"Serves v1.1 Chunks"| UserNew["New Users on v1.1"]
```

---

## Historical Retention & Ring Buffer Garbage Collection

To ensure disk usage remains bounded, `nextdeployd` maintains an immutable ring buffer of the 5 most recent releases in `/opt/nextdeploy/apps/<app>/releases/`. Older release directories are automatically retired and cleaned up during atomic cutover, while active chunks in `shared_static` remain available to avoid missing chunk 404s.

meta.title: nextdeployd VPS Daemon
meta.lede: The high-performance static Go systems agent running on Linux hosts, supervising releases, systemd units, socket arbitration, and zero-downtime cutovers.

vps/daemon.body:
## Systems Architecture of `nextdeployd`

`nextdeployd` is a lightweight, statically linked Go binary compiled with zero external C-library dependencies. It runs as a persistent systemd service on your managed Linux host (`/usr/local/bin/nextdeployd`).

Unlike heavyweight orchestration systems (Kubernetes Kubelet, Nomad, Docker Daemon), `nextdeployd` consumes **under 12 MB of RAM** at idle and communicates with the `nextdeploy` CLI via an encrypted SSH channel or authenticated mTLS Unix socket.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    CLI["nextdeploy CLI on Dev / CI"] -->|"SSH / SFTP + HMAC-SHA256"| Daemon["nextdeployd Go Daemon"]
    Daemon --> FS["Directory Layout Engine: /opt/nextdeploy/apps/app"]
    Daemon --> DBus["systemd Unit & Process Supervisor"]
    Daemon --> CaddyCtl["Caddy Sandbox Validate & Reload"]
    Daemon --> Prober["Dual-Stage TCP & HTTP Health Prober"]
    Daemon --> Audit["Redacted JSON Audit Log (0600)"]
```

---

## Daemon Responsibilities & Lifecycle

### 1. Release Ingestion & SHA256 Verification
When `nextdeploy ship` transmits a new release archive:
- The daemon unpacks the tarball into `/opt/nextdeploy/apps/<app>/releases/<timestamp>/`.
- Computes and verifies SHA256 integrity checksums against the manifest.
- Copies fresh static JavaScript chunks into `/opt/nextdeploy/apps/<app>/shared_static/`.

### 2. Dynamic Port Arbitration
- Inspects active listening ports starting from base port `3000`.
- Assigns an available loopback port (e.g. `3001`, `3002`) to the incoming release.
- Generates an isolated `.env.production` containing `PORT=3002` and runtime variables.

### 3. Dual-Stage Health Verification
Before cutting over any traffic:
- **Stage 1 (TCP Socket Listener):** Polls the assigned loopback port until the Node.js server actively binds and accepts incoming TCP connections.
- **Stage 2 (HTTP Health Probe):** Issues HTTP GET requests to `http://127.0.0.1:3002/api/health` verifying HTTP 200 OK within the configured timeout window.

### 4. Atomic Cutover Execution
- Issues an atomic POSIX symlink swap (`rename()`) pointing `/opt/nextdeploy/apps/<app>/current` to the new release directory.
- Sends an updated upstream configuration JSON to Caddy's live admin API (`http://127.0.0.1:2019/load`).
- Caddy hot-swaps traffic routing instantly (<2ms) without dropping active TCP connections.

### 5. Historical Retention & Ring Buffer Garbage Collection
- Maintains an immutable ring buffer of the 5 most recent releases.
- Older releases are automatically pruned to prevent disk bloat, while `shared_static` chunks are preserved.

---

## systemd Unit Configuration (`nextdeployd.service`)

The daemon runs under systemd with automatic restart on failure:

```ini
[Unit]
Description=NextDeploy Systems Host Daemon
After=network.target caddy.service
Requires=caddy.service

[Service]
Type=simple
User=root
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/nextdeployd --foreground=true
Restart=always
RestartSec=5s
LimitNOFILE=65536
StandardOutput=journal
StandardError=journal

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
```

---

## Daemon Hot-Upgrade Protocol (`nextdeploy upgrade-daemon`)

To upgrade `nextdeployd` on your remote Linux VPS to match your local CLI version without restarting active Next.js user applications:

```bash
nextdeploy upgrade-daemon
```

### Upgrade Execution Steps:
1. CLI uploads the new static binary to `/usr/local/bin/nextdeployd.new`.
2. Verifies cryptographic signature and file permissions.
3. Performs an atomic swap: `mv /usr/local/bin/nextdeployd.new /usr/local/bin/nextdeployd`.
4. Executes `systemctl restart nextdeployd`.
5. Active Next.js processes and Caddy proxy routing continue running with zero downtime.

meta.title: Go Sidecar
meta.lede: Optional high-performance Go reverse proxy sitting between Caddy and Next.js on VPS deployments — serves prerendered HTML/RSC payloads in sub-millisecond latency and offloads image optimization from Node.js.

vps/go-sidecar.body:
## Why Use the Go Sidecar

In a standard Node.js VPS deployment, Node's single-threaded event loop handles dynamic SSR, prerendered HTML/RSC serving, and CPU-heavy `/_next/image` transcoding all at once.

NextDeploy's optional Go sidecar sits between Caddy and your Next.js Node server:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Caddy["Caddy (:443)"] -->|"lb_policy first"| Sidecar["Go Sidecar"]
    Sidecar -->|"Prerendered HTML / RSC"| Cache["Sub-ms In-Memory Cache"]
    Sidecar -->|"/_next/image"| Img["Multi-Threaded Go Image Transcoder"]
    Sidecar -->|"Dynamic SSR / API / Middleware"| Node["Next.js Standalone (Node)"]
    Caddy -.->|"Health Failover"| Node
```

The sidecar is an acceleration layer, not a replacement for Next.js. Any route that needs runtime rendering, middleware, or dynamic execution passes straight through to Node.js over HTTP/1.1 keep-alive connections.

## Capabilities

- **In-Memory Prerendered HTML & RSC Cache:** Indexes static build outputs into a radix tree and serves eligible HTML and `.rsc` payloads without waking Node.js.
- **Multi-Threaded Image Optimization:** Handles `/_next/image?url=...&w=...&q=...` on a dedicated Go worker pool (resizing and WebP/AVIF/JPEG transcoding with local caching) so image processing never blocks Node's event loop.
- **Transparent Fallback:** Unsupported routes, dynamic queries, Server Actions, and middleware pass directly through to Node.js.

## Enabling in `nextdeploy.yml`

The Go sidecar is available for `target_type: vps` deployments:

```yaml
target_type: vps

app:
  name: my-nextjs-app
  environment: production
  domain: app.example.com
  port: 3000
  gosidecar:
    enabled: true
    image_optimization: true
    isr_cache: true
    max_image_workers: 4
```

Then deploy as usual:

```bash
nextdeploy prepare   # first-time VPS setup
nextdeploy ship      # deploys Node + Go sidecar + Caddy routing
```

meta.title: VPS Overview
meta.lede: Bare-metal Next.js hosting on any Linux VPS with Caddy auto-TLS, nextdeployd atomic releases, cgroup v2 sandboxing, cumulative chunk pooling, and optional Go sidecar acceleration.

vps/overview.body:
## Why Bare-Metal Linux VPS

Running Next.js directly on a $4–$20/month Linux VPS (Hetzner, DigitalOcean, Linode, OVH, or AWS EC2) eliminates Docker daemon overhead, container networking bottlenecks, cold starts, and per-invocation serverless billing — while keeping complete developer simplicity:

1. **Caddy Reverse Proxy:** Automatic Let's Encrypt TLS, HTTP/2 & HTTP/3, and direct NVMe `sendfile` delivery of `/_next/static/*` and `public/*`.
2. **`nextdeployd` Daemon:** Lightweight Go systems agent managing release directories, systemd units, dual-stage TCP + HTTP health probes, atomic symlink swaps, and instant rollbacks.
3. **Cumulative Chunk Pooling (`shared_static`):** Prevents `ChunkLoadError` 404 crashes for active browser tabs across releases.
4. **Optional Go Sidecar (`gosidecar`):** Sub-millisecond prerendered HTML/RSC serving and multi-threaded Go WebP/AVIF image transcoding ahead of Node.js.
5. **Kernel `cgroup v2` Isolation:** Hard memory and CPU limits per application prevent noisy neighbor issues.

---

## Host & Access Requirements

Before running `nextdeploy prepare` or `nextdeploy ship` on a VPS, ensure you have:

1. **Ubuntu/Debian Linux VPS:** Public IPv4 with ports `22` (SSH), `80` (HTTP/ACME), and `443` (HTTPS) open.
2. **Non-root `sudo` user:** A non-root SSH user (e.g. `deploy` or `ubuntu`) with `sudo` privileges (`nextdeploy prepare` refuses `root` by default).
3. **SSH private key path:** A local SSH private key (`~/.ssh/id_ed25519`, `chmod 600`) configured as `key_path` in `nextdeploy.yml` with its public key installed in the remote user's `~/.ssh/authorized_keys`.
4. **Domain DNS:** An `A` record pointing your domain to the VPS IPv4 address so Caddy can provision Let's Encrypt TLS certificates.
5. **Secrets synchronization:** Sync full-stack runtime secrets via **Doppler (recommended)** (`doppler run -- nextdeploy secrets sync`) or **`.env`** (`nextdeploy secrets load .env.production && nextdeploy secrets sync`).

See the [Requirements Guide](/docs/getting-started/requirements) for setup commands.

---

## Target Architecture Layout

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Client["Incoming Users (HTTPS :443)"] --> Caddy["Caddy Reverse Proxy + Coraza WAF"]
    Caddy -->|"/_next/static/* (immutable)"| Static["shared_static/ Chunk Pool"]
    Caddy -->|"public/* (must-revalidate)"| Public["Active Release public/"]
    Caddy -->|"HTTP (lb_policy first)"| Sidecar["Go Sidecar (Optional: HTML/RSC Cache & /_next/image)"]
    Sidecar -->|"Dynamic SSR / API / Actions"| Node["Next.js Release (127.0.0.1:port)"]
    Caddy -.->|"Direct / Health Failover"| Node
    Caddy -->|"audit.log & access.log"| Fail2Ban["Fail2Ban (caddy-waf jail)"]
    CLI["nextdeploy CLI"] -->|"SSH / SFTP + HMAC-SHA256"| Daemon["nextdeployd Daemon (systemd)"]
    Daemon -->|"Manages Embedded Sidecar"| Sidecar
    Daemon -->|"TCP + HTTP Health Probe & systemd"| Node
    Daemon -->|"Atomic current.tmp -> current"| Releases["/opt/nextdeploy/apps/app/releases/"]
    Daemon -->|"Sandbox Validate & Reload"| Caddy
```

---

## Directory Layout on the Host Server

NextDeploy organizes applications under `/opt/nextdeploy/apps/<app-name>/`:

```text
/opt/nextdeploy/apps/<app-name>/
├── current -> releases/1763890000-a1b2c3d/   # Atomically swapped POSIX symlink
├── port                                       # Persisted active loopback port
├── releases/
│   ├── 1763880000-9f8e7d6/                    # Retained release n-1 (instant rollback)
│   └── 1763890000-a1b2c3d/                    # Current active release ({unix-ts}-{shortSha})
│       ├── .next/standalone/server.js
│       ├── .env.nextdeploy                      # Rendered secrets (0600, nextdeploy:nextdeploy)
│       └── .nextdeploy/
│           ├── metadata.json
│           └── node.port
└── shared_static/                             # Cumulative pool of content-hashed JS/CSS chunks
    └── chunks/
        ├── app/layout-1a2b3c.js
        └── pages/index-4d5e6f.js
```

---

## Core Operational Commands

```bash
# 1. Bootstrap fresh server (installs Caddy, nextdeployd, configures systemd)
nextdeploy prepare

# 2. Dry run preview of planned changes and disk allocation
nextdeploy plan

# 3. Build locally, sync assets, execute health checks, and cut over
nextdeploy ship

# 4. View real-time service status, memory/CPU usage, active release
nextdeploy status

# 5. Tail live logs across application and reverse proxy
nextdeploy logs

# 6. Instant zero-downtime rollback to previous release (<10ms)
nextdeploy rollback

# 7. Hot-upgrade remote nextdeployd daemon to match CLI version
nextdeploy upgrade-daemon
```

---

## Security & Sandboxing

On VPS targets, NextDeploy configures systemd services with strict Linux kernel sandboxing:
- `User=nextdeploy` / `Group=nextdeploy`: Dedicated unprivileged system account (`--shell /sbin/nologin`) with `ReadWritePaths` scoped to the release directory.
- `ProtectSystem=strict`: Root filesystem is mounted read-only for the application process.
- `ProtectHome=yes`: `/home` and `/root` are inaccessible to the Node.js process.
- `PrivateTmp=yes` & `NoNewPrivileges=yes`: Isolated `/tmp` namespace and blocked privilege escalation.
- Opt-in `cgroup v2` limits (`MemoryMax`, `MemoryHigh`, `CPUQuota`): Configured via `app.resources` in `nextdeploy.yml`.

meta.title: Instant VPS Rollbacks
meta.lede: Sub-second traffic rollback on bare-metal servers using atomic symlink pointer swaps and release ring buffers without rebuilding.

vps/rollback.body:
## Overview

When an unexpected regression or runtime crash occurs in production, rebuilding and redeploying can take minutes. 

On Linux VPS targets, NextDeploy executes rollbacks in **under 200 milliseconds** by maintaining a **5-release ring buffer** and flipping the active directory symlink atomically.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Current["current Symlink -> Release v12"]
    Buffer["Release Ring Buffer on Disk (keep = 5)"]
    Buffer --> Rel10["Release v10: /opt/nextdeploy/apps/app/releases/10"]
    Buffer --> Rel11["Release v11: /opt/nextdeploy/apps/app/releases/11"]
    Buffer --> Rel12["Release v12: /opt/nextdeploy/apps/app/releases/12 ACTIVE"]

    RollbackCmd["nextdeploy rollback"] --> Switch["Flip Symlink Atomically: current -> Release v11"]
    Switch --> Signal["Health Probe, Caddy Reload & Drain Old Unit"]
    Signal --> Complete["Traffic Serving Release v11 Zero-Downtime"]
```

---

## The Release Ring Buffer

Every successful `nextdeploy ship` installs the deployment into a unique, timestamped release directory on the VPS:

```
/opt/nextdeploy/apps/<app>/
├── current -> releases/20261123_142010 (Active POSIX Symlink)
├── releases/
│   ├── 20261123_110500  (Release v10)
│   ├── 20261123_121530  (Release v11)
│   ├── 20261123_133045  (Release v12 - Previous Stable)
│   └── 20261123_142010  (Release v13 - Current Active)
└── shared_static/       (Cumulative pooled Next.js JS chunks)
```

- **Ring Buffer Retention**: The `nextdeployd` daemon preserves the last 5 successful release directories.
- **Automated Pruning**: Older releases beyond the retention window are cleanly pruned from disk, while their static JS chunks remain preserved in `shared_static` to protect active browser sessions.

---

## Executing Rollbacks

### 1. Roll Back to Immediately Preceding Release
```bash
nextdeploy rollback
```

### 2. Roll Back Multiple Versions
```bash
# Roll back 2 releases back
nextdeploy rollback --steps 2
```

### 3. Roll Back to a Specific Release ID
```bash
nextdeploy rollback --release 20261123_121530
```

---

## Rollback Lifecycle & Safety Guarantees

When `nextdeploy rollback` is triggered:
1. **Target Inspection**: The CLI queries `nextdeployd` for the active release history.
2. **Health Verification**: Before traffic cutover, the target release process is started on an isolated port and probed (`GET /api/health`).
3. **Atomic Symlink Flip**: `nextdeployd` creates a temporary symlink (`current.tmp`) pointing to the target release and renames it over `current` using the atomic POSIX `rename()` syscall.
4. **Zero Dropped Packets**: Caddy's dynamic upstream reloader gracefully finishes in-flight requests on the old process before routing new TCP connections to the rolled-back version.

meta.title: systemd Hardening & cgroup v2 Sandboxing
meta.lede: Production process sandboxing, Linux kernel memory caps, unprivileged DynamicUser, and filesystem lockdown.

vps/systemd-hardening.body:
## Why Bare-Metal Needs Hardening

Deploying Node.js applications directly on a bare-metal Linux server without Docker containers can raise security concerns if applications are run as `root` or unconstrained users.

NextDeploy achieves **container-level isolation with bare-metal speed** by leveraging native Linux kernel primitives and **systemd security sandboxing**.

---

## Applied Security Directives

Every Next.js application service generated by NextDeploy (`/etc/systemd/system/nextdeploy-<app>.service`) enforces strict isolation:

```ini
[Unit]
Description=NextDeploy App - %i
After=network.target

[Service]
Type=simple
WorkingDirectory=/opt/nextdeploy/apps/%i/current

# ─── 1. Identity & Privilege Isolation ───
DynamicUser=yes
User=nextdeploy-%i
Group=nextdeploy-%i
NoNewPrivileges=yes

# ─── 2. Filesystem Lockdown ───
ProtectSystem=strict
ProtectHome=yes
PrivateTmp=yes
PrivateDevices=yes
ProtectKernelTunables=yes
ProtectKernelModules=yes
ProtectControlGroups=yes
ReadWritePaths=/opt/nextdeploy/apps/%i/current/.next/cache

# ─── 3. Network & Capability Restrictions ───
CapabilityBoundingSet=
AmbientCapabilities=
RestrictAddressFamilies=AF_UNIX AF_INET AF_INET6
RestrictNamespaces=yes

# ─── 4. Kernel cgroup v2 Resource Caps ───
MemoryMax=1G
MemoryHigh=850M
CPUQuota=200%
TasksMax=256

Restart=always
RestartSec=5s
```

---

## Directives Breakdown

### 1. `DynamicUser=yes`
NextDeploy allocates an ephemeral, unprivileged UID/GID from the dynamic user range (`61184-65519`) when the service starts, and deallocates it when stopped.
- The service does not have a permanent entry in `/etc/passwd`.
- The process cannot write to any system directory outside explicitly declared `ReadWritePaths`.

### 2. `ProtectSystem=strict` & `PrivateTmp=yes`
- The entire operating system filesystem hierarchy (`/usr`, `/boot`, `/etc`) is mounted **read-only** for the application process.
- `/tmp` is placed in an isolated per-process namespace, preventing cross-tenant leakage or temp file attacks.

### 3. Linux Kernel `cgroup v2` Memory Limits
- `MemoryMax=1G`: If a memory leak occurs, the Linux kernel terminates only the leaky Node.js worker rather than crashing the entire VPS host (preventing OOM panics).
- `CPUQuota=200%`: Limits compute consumption to 2 vCPUs, preventing CPU starvation for Caddy or sibling applications.
